title: Shift and Capitals
summary: Capital letters with Shift held by the opposite hand, so neither hand has to twist.

explain.goal: Type capital letters by holding Shift with the pinky of the opposite hand.
why: Shift is a modifier: you hold it while you press another key. Using the pinky on the opposite hand from the letter means neither hand has to twist or stretch.
If you capitalize a letter on the left with the left Shift, the same hand has to do two jobs at once, and it cramps.
So the rule is simple: letter on the left, Shift on the right. Letter on the right, Shift on the left.
how: For a left-hand letter, hold Shift with your right pinky, press the letter, and let go.
For a right-hand letter, hold Shift with your left pinky, press the letter, and let go.
Let go of Shift straight away, so the next letter is lowercase.

mistakes.mistake: Using the Shift key on the same side as the letter
mistakes.reason: One hand has to press two keys at once, which twists your wrist and slows you down.
The next letter comes out capitalized too, and you have to fix it.

explain.recap: Shift with the pinky of the hand that is not typing the letter. Hold, press, release.
